findings.title: Phase 4e's docstring and Phase 7's banner both claim the "NOT paused" property is asserted, but no `require(!v2.paused())` exists in Phase 7 or in VerifyPromotionReady
findings.description: `_phase4e_phlimboV3Cutover`'s docstring at :1643-1645 states of the no-pause and no-promotion properties: "NOT DONE ANYWHERE IN HERE, both deliberate and both asserted in Phase 7". Phase 7 does assert the no-promotion negative (`promoToken() == 0`, `promoPhase() == None`, :2407-2408) but carries no pause assertion at all: the section is only a banner comment `// ---- V2 wound down, NOT paused. ----` (:2418) plus a console line "PhlimboV2: ... NOT paused" (:2454). Exhaustive grep over both script files shows the only V2 pause check in the whole suite is `require(!v2.paused(), ...)` at :1748-1751, which sits INSIDE `if (!_isConfigured("p4e_migrate"))` and is therefore skipped on every resume leg, and is never reachable from `VerifyPromotionReady` (which overrides `run()` and calls Phase 7 only). Consequence: the post-broadcast verifier prints "NOT paused" for a PhlimboV2 that someone paused after the cutover, and a resume leg that has already completed the migration never checks the property at all.
findings.impact: A verification log line and a phase docstring both assert a property that nothing proves. On its own the impact is small — a paused V2 at `totalStaked == 0` traps nobody — but this is comment drift inside the one control surface whose entire purpose (story 075, ledger M-01 `2c53e944ca`) is to replace unticked human checklist lines with executable assertions. A reader auditing the cutover from the logs would conclude the property was machine-verified.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json.assertionCoverage.pauseAssertion; grep of `paused()` across script/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol + script/VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol returns only :775 (a console.log), :1749 (inside the p4e_migrate gate), and the unrelated Phase 4d/6 old-contract pauses at :1596-1597 / :2165-2166. Independently identified by story 076's own Review Results issue 1 (lines 825-833) and carried forward under Auto-Completed as a [low] that the human confirmation at lines 896-901 does NOT cover — only the conservation [medium] was accepted. SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS, found in my own dry run and not previously recorded: the cutover summary block prints `phUSD minter-set DELTA (story 076): +PhlimboV3, -PhlimboV2. Nothing else moved.` unconditionally on every run, including a broadcast, even though the same run's own Phase 0 output five screens earlier reads `V2 holds phUSD mint: false` and `membership mask: 270080` — i.e. the `-PhlimboV2` half is a no-op. The VERIFIER handles this correctly with a conditional NOTE (VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:259-263); the deploy script's summary does not.
findings.recommendation: Add `require(!IPhlimboV2Like(PHLIMBO_V2).paused(), "PhlimboV2 is paused - the migration cannot be trusted and the log below would be false")` to `_phase7_phlimboV3Assertions` next to the existing `desiredAPYBps() == 0` check at :2419. It is `view`, so `VerifyPromotionReady` inherits it for free, which is exactly the property story 076 relied on for every other Phase 7 addition. If the owner prefers to allow a post-cutover pause, delete the "NOT paused" claim from :1643-1645 and the log at :2454 instead — but do not leave both. Separately, make the summary's `-PhlimboV2` line conditional on `phusdMinterMaskAtPhase0 & (1 << PHUSD_MINTER_BIT_PHLIMBO_V2) != 0`, mirroring the NOTE the verifier already prints at VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:259-263, so the deploy log and the verify log stop disagreeing about whether a revoke happened.

findings.title: PhlimboV3's committed APY is proven only inside the `_isConfigured` gate a resume skips; neither Phase 7 nor VerifyPromotionReady ever reads `v3.desiredAPYBps()` or `v3.apySetInProgress()`
findings.description: Story 076 Autonomous Decision 2 correctly identifies that `desiredAPYBps() == bps` is a vacuous read-back when `bps == 0` (both real cases here), and adds `require(!p.apySetInProgress())` at :1826-1832 so a missed 100-block commit window fails loudly. That non-vacuous proof lives entirely inside `_setDesiredAPYTwoStep`, which Phase 4e calls only from within `if (!_isConfigured("p4e_v3_apy"))` (:1684-1688). `_trackConfig("p4e_v3_apy")` is stamped into the progress file during forge's LOCAL pass (`_trackConfig` -> `_writeProgressFileWithStatus`, :3009-3015), i.e. BEFORE either `setDesiredAPY` transaction is dispatched. If the second (commit) transaction is rejected or dropped on the Ledger, the progress file already records the step as done, a `:resume` skips it, and PhlimboV3 is left latched mid-preview with the APY uncommitted. Grep over both script files confirms `v3.desiredAPYBps()` appears nowhere in Phase 7 or `VerifyPromotionReady` (:2419 checks V2 only), and `apySetInProgress()` appears nowhere outside `_setDesiredAPYTwoStep`. Phase 8's `_probePhlimboV3StakeClaim` cannot substitute: it is preview-only AND it deliberately ARMS its own 1000-bps probe APY whenever it reads 0 (:2530-2535), so it masks exactly this failure.
findings.impact: Today the mirrored target is 0 (verified live: `PhlimboV2.desiredAPYBps() == 0`), so a missed commit leaves V3 at 0 — the same value it was going to be set to, and the impact is confined to a stuck `apySetInProgress` latch. The defect is structural, not conditional: if V2's APY is ever retuned non-zero before the Ledger session (the script deliberately mirrors it live, :1685), a resume leg would leave PhlimboV3 emitting nothing while every post-cutover assertion and the whole verifier report read green. That is the exact silent-failure shape story 076 exists to close on the mint side.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json.assertionCoverage.v3ApyAssertion; grep of `desiredAPYBps|apySetInProgress` over script/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol and script/VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol (full result set, not truncated) — the only assertions are :1823/:1827 (inside the setter) and :2419 (V2 only). Live read at block 25678182: `PhlimboV2.desiredAPYBps() == 0`, `apySetInProgress() == false`.
findings.recommendation: Add two `view` assertions to `_phase7_phlimboV3Assertions` so `VerifyPromotionReady` inherits them: `require(!IPhlimboAPYLike(newPhlimboV3).apySetInProgress(), "PhlimboV3 left latched mid-preview - the APY commit never landed")` and `require(IPhlimboAPYLike(newPhlimboV3).desiredAPYBps() == IPhlimboV2Like(PHLIMBO_V2).desiredAPYBps(), "PhlimboV3 APY does not mirror V2's")`. Note the second must be sequenced against step 11 (which zeroes V2), so either capture the mirrored target as a write-once baseline alongside `phlimboV2StakedAtCutover`, or assert only the latch. Add the same `!apySetInProgress()` check for PhlimboV2 next to the existing :2419 check.

findings.title: `baselines.phusdMinterMask` is the one write-once baseline with no resume abort, so a resume leg silently re-derives a POST-cutover mask and the two-sided delta self-certifies
findings.description: The suite now carries three write-once baselines. Two are mechanically protected against a hand-trimmed progress file: `bptAtCutover` (story 074) and `phlimboV2StakedAtCutover`, whose Phase 0 has an explicit `require(!_isConfigured("p4e_migrate") || phlimboBaselineFromProgressFile, "RESUME ABORT: ...")` at :798-801, precisely because re-deriving it from an emptied V2 would make the conservation assertion vacuous. The third — `phusdMinterMask` / `phusdMintVersion`, which story 076 promoted from a supporting record to the load-bearing input of the two-sided delta — has no such guard. `_snapshotPhusdMinterSet` (:974-997) returns early only when `phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile` is already true; otherwise it records the LIVE mask unconditionally, with no reference to whether `p4e_v3_mintGrant` / `p4e_v2_mintRevoke` have already run. A `:resume` whose progress file lost the `baselines` block therefore stamps a post-cutover mask as the Phase 0 baseline and writes it straight back out; `VerifyPromotionReady._verifyMintAuthorityInvariance` then sees `phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile == true` (:230-233 satisfied), compares live against a baseline taken from the same post-cutover state, and passes `liveMask == baseline & ~v2Bit` trivially — bit 19 is already clear on both sides after the revoke.
findings.impact: A green `promotion-ready:verify` that proves nothing about the phUSD mint-authority delta — the single control story 076 added to replace story 072's now-false 'minter set byte-identical' invariant, and the one the operator is told (`:232`) is verified NOWHERE ELSE. It fails open, not closed. Reaching it requires an operator hand-trim error on the resume path, which the docs warn against in prose (`:800`, `:171-173`) — but the identical risk on the two sibling baselines was considered serious enough to guard in code, so the asymmetry is the defect.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json.assertionCoverage.baselineGuards — a three-way comparison of the guards on `bptAtCutover`, `phlimboV2StakedAtCutover` (:798-801 deploy-side abort + :190-200 verifier abort) and `phusdMinterMask` (verifier abort at :230-233 only, no deploy-side abort). Prior art in the same ledger: L-02 `4fd1642310` ("Phase 7's BPT conservation assertion degrades to `>= 0` on every resume path") is the same class on a different baseline; this is disclosed as lineage, not presented as a fresh discovery — the mechanism differs (silent re-derivation of a post-state baseline vs. degradation to a zero baseline) and the affected control is new in story 076.
findings.recommendation: Mirror :798-801 verbatim for the mint-authority baseline: in `_phase0_preconditions`, immediately after `_snapshotPhusdMinterSet()`, add `require(!(_isConfigured("p4e_v3_mintGrant") || _isConfigured("p4e_v2_mintRevoke")) || phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile, "RESUME ABORT: a phUSD setMinter step is already configured but the progress file carries no baselines.phusdMinterMask - restore that block verbatim; re-deriving it post-cutover makes the two-sided delta vacuous")`. Optionally also refuse to overwrite when `phusdMinterBaselineRecorded` would be taken after any Phase 4e mutation.

findings.title: The `totalStaked() == 0` completeness gate that makes `phUSD.setMinter(PHLIMBO_V2, false)` safe is evaluated in forge's local pass, so it constrains pre-broadcast state, not the state the revoke actually lands in
findings.description: Story 076 Concerns §3 and the inline comment at :1785-1790 argue the V2 mint revoke is safe because two facts hold at the moment it executes: `totalStaked == 0` (so `PhlimboV2._claimRewards` early-returns before its BARE, REVERTING `phUSD.mint` at PhlimboV2.sol:495) and `desiredAPYBps == 0` (so a late staker accrues nothing). Both are enforced by statements that forge evaluates during its single LOCAL execution pass, before transaction #1 is dispatched (the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast property established by run-23 and documented for this suite in the `:verify` npm doc key). Under `--slow --ledger` the actual broadcast runs for minutes across many blocks, and `PhlimboV2.stake` is ungated and — by this story's own deliberate design — unpausable. So the gate at :1779 is a statement about the fork state at signing time; the `setMinter(PHLIMBO_V2, false)` transaction lands later against state the gate never saw. `VerifyPromotionReady` does re-check `v2.totalStaked() == 0` live (:2420), but only AFTER the revoke has already landed — it detects, it does not gate.
findings.impact: A user who stakes into PhlimboV2 during the broadcast window, after Phase 4e's last `migrate` transaction and while V2 still carries a non-zero APY, accrues pending phUSD that V2 can no longer mint once the revoke lands, and their `withdraw` reverts — freezing principal, which is precisely the failure the gate is documented as preventing. The window is empty today and I verified that empirically, not by assumption: `PhlimboV2.desiredAPYBps() == 0`, `phUSDPerSecond() == 0` and `accPhUSDPerShare() == 0` at block 25678182, so no position can accrue pending phUSD and no late staker can either. The finding is the ordering property, and the escalation trigger is concrete: if V2's `desiredAPYBps` is non-zero at cutover time (the script mirrors it live at :1685, so it is not pinned), this becomes a live principal-freeze vector and should be re-weighed as Medium.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json.localPassOrdering; live reads at block 25678182 recorded in side-effects.json.liveChainReads (`desiredAPYBps`, `phUSDPerSecond`, `accPhUSDPerShare` all 0). Ledger lineage disclosed: M-01 `2c53e944ca` (fix-pending) covers the ABSENCE of post-broadcast verification, which story 075 remedied with `VerifyPromotionReady`; this is the distinct residual — a safety GATE whose ordering the verifier cannot restore, because verification after the fact is not gating.
findings.recommendation: Two options, both cheap. (a) Re-order so the revoke can never precede a live check: split `phUSD.setMinter(PHLIMBO_V2, false)` out of Phase 4e into a separate, separately-signed follow-up key run after `promotion-ready:verify` has confirmed `totalStaked() == 0` against live post-broadcast state. (b) Make the revoke self-gating on chain by routing it through a tiny helper that reads `PhlimboV2.totalStaked()` and reverts if non-zero in the same transaction as the `setMinter` call, so the gate and the mutation are atomic. Additionally, add a Phase 0 `require(IPhlimboV2Like(PHLIMBO_V2).desiredAPYBps() == 0)` so the safe case is pinned rather than merely observed, and the script refuses to run in the configuration where this bites.
findings.dedupDecision: KEPT — distinct defect, NOT a restatement of ledger L-03 ea648ec5ea
findings.dedupReasoning: Explicitly adjudicated per rule 3. Both are ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast descendants, but the family is a MECHANISM, not a finding — this ledger already carries five members filed individually (ea648ec5ea, 3c957109ef, 2212c1c4e8, 5c6d2c9e3b, and M-01 2c53e944ca), so per-control filing is the project s own established precedent and collapsing here would be inconsistent with it. Substantively: L-03 concerns a STATUS FLAG written to an off-chain progress file before the event it attests, whose victim is the patch script s own gate. PR24-04 concerns an ON-CHAIN SAFETY GATE (require(v2.totalStaked()==0)) whose victim is a late PhlimboV2 staker whose principal freezes when the setMinter revoke lands. Different artifact, different victim, different impact ceiling (PR24-04 carries a concrete escalation trigger to Medium if V2 desiredAPYBps is non-zero at cutover; L-03 has none). Remediations do not overlap at all: L-03 is fixed by stamping status after broadcast; PR24-04 is fixed by splitting the revoke into a separately-signed post-verify key or by making it atomically self-gating on chain. Fixing L-03 leaves the freeze window untouched. Also distinct from M-01 2c53e944ca, which PR24-04 already discloses: M-01 is the absence of post-broadcast verification and was answered by story 075 s VerifyPromotionReady; PR24-04 is the residual that verification structurally CANNOT answer, because a check that runs after the revoke detects but does not gate.

findings.title: Phase 0 never establishes that PhlimboV2 can mint phUSD during the migration, yet every migrated position with pending phUSD routes through V2's bare, reverting `phUSD.mint`
findings.description: `MigratorV2V3.migrateOne` migrates a user by calling `phlimboV2.withdraw(amount, user)`, which runs `PhlimboV2._claimRewards` (:486) and pays the phUSD leg with a BARE, reverting `phUSD.mint(beneficiary, pendingPhUSDAmount)` (:495) whenever `pendingPhUSDAmount > 0`. V3's non-reverting `try`/bank was added by phlimbo story 029 to V3 ONLY. So the migration's per-user body silently depends on PhlimboV2 holding an active phUSD mint grant for any position carrying pending phUSD. Phase 0 reads that grant and LOGS it (:784-787, `console.log("  V2 holds phUSD mint:  ", ...)`) but never requires it, and Phase 4e's step 14 only ever revokes it. Because `migrateOne` runs inside `migrate`'s try/catch, a revert here is absorbed into `UserMigrationSkipped` and the cursor advances — so the failure is a silent skip, not an error, and the hard `require(v2.totalStaked() == 0)` gate at :1779 then aborts the ENTIRE promotion-ready cutover on behalf of a defect three contracts away.
findings.impact: Latent, not live, and I verified that on chain rather than assuming it: `phUSD.authorizedMinters(PhlimboV2)` reads `(false, 0)` and `PhlimboV2.accPhUSDPerShare()` reads 0 at block 25678182, so no live position carries pending phUSD and the dependency is currently dormant — consistent with the dry run migrating all 16 users with zero skips. Were V2's APY ever armed between now and the Ledger session (which also re-arms accrual on existing positions), every position with pending phUSD would be skipped, the gate would abort the whole cutover, and the operator's only diagnostic would be raw revert bytes in `UserMigrationSkipped`. Because the abort happens in the local pass this is a liveness/operational footgun, not asset risk — nothing broadcasts.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json.liveChainReads (authorizedMinters(PhlimboV2) = false/0; accPhUSDPerShare = 0; phUSDPerSecond = 0; desiredAPYBps = 0, all at block 25678182); lib/phlimbo-ea/src/PhlimboV2.sol:486-495 (bare mint) vs lib/phlimbo-ea/src/MigratorV2V3.sol:172-211 (try/catch absorbs it, cursor advances).
findings.recommendation: Add a Phase 0 precondition that makes the dependency explicit and self-diagnosing rather than leaving it to a log line: `require(IPhlimboV2Like(PHLIMBO_V2).accPhUSDPerShare() == 0 || _v2HoldsPhusdMint(), "PhlimboV2 has advanced accPhUSDPerShare but holds no phUSD mint authority - every position carrying pending phUSD will be SILENTLY SKIPPED by migrateOne and the totalStaked()==0 gate will abort the cutover. Grant it before Phase 4e and let step 14 revoke it afterwards")`. This costs nothing today (both sides read 0) and turns an unexplained whole-cutover abort into a one-line diagnosis.

findings.title: Story 076 Concerns §4 states both deposit views are bound to PhlimboV2; the ViewRouter-registered `DepositPageView` is in fact bound to PhlimboV1, so the recorded follow-up would move the live UI onto a staler view
findings.description: Story 076 Concerns §4 declares the view layer out of scope on the stated premise that "both views are bound to V2, and the live deposit UI is on the deprecated one", and records two follow-ups on that basis: (a) redeploy `DepositPageView` against V3, (b) move phlimbo-ui's deposit page onto ViewRouter resolution "the way the mint page already is". The premise is wrong for the router-registered surface. Read live at block 25678182: `ViewRouter(0xC17Ce1cE...).pages(keccak256("deposit"))` resolves to `DepositPageView 0x50D4443782bB9A6e8D65dAcd593684EDd3FF03b8`, whose immutable `phlimbo()` reads `0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4` — PhlimboV1, not PhlimboV2 `0x6084a02C...`. Only the deprecated `DepositView 0x0725722b...` was redeployed against V2 (`mainnet-addresses.ts:12`, story 049 follow-up); `DepositPageView` was left on V1. So the ViewRouter deposit page is already one generation stale TODAY, pre-cutover, and will be two generations stale after Phase 4e.
findings.impact: Two consequences the story's out-of-scope decision did not price in. First, follow-up (b) as written is actively harmful ordering: moving phlimbo-ui's deposit page onto ViewRouter resolution before follow-up (a) lands would migrate users from a V2-correct view onto a V1-stale one, so the recommended sequencing must be (a) then (b), not either order. Second, post-cutover the deprecated `DepositView` the live UI actually reads points at a PhlimboV2 the cutover has deliberately emptied to `totalStaked == 0`, so every migrated user's deposit page reads a zero balance while their principal sits in PhlimboV3. That is a user-visible zero-balance display across the entire migrated user base for as long as the redeploy is outstanding. No asset is at risk — this is a display and operational-sequencing issue, and the redeploy itself is legitimately out of scope for a script-and-tooling story.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json.liveChainReads.viewLayer: `ViewRouter.pages(keccak256("deposit")) == 0x50D4443782bB9A6e8D65dAcd593684EDd3FF03b8`; `DepositPageView.phlimbo() == 0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4`; `DepositView.phlimbo() == 0x6084a02C2Ac0127ddF1e617De257c61480A2AeE0`; `PhlimboV1(0x3984...).totalStaked() == 13615682000000000000000`. Both views bake `IPhlimbo public immutable phlimbo` (src/views/DepositPageView.sol:9, src/views/DepositView.sol:21). The two follow-ups DO exist in ~/code/product-owner/story-dependencies.md line 222, but as an HTML comment marked "not yet a story" with no numbered dependency row — tracked, not raised.
findings.recommendation: Correct the premise in the follow-up record at story-dependencies.md:222 — `DepositPageView` is on PhlimboV1, not V2 — and state the ordering constraint explicitly: the phStaging2 redeploy + `ViewRouter.setPage("deposit", ...)` re-registration MUST land before the phlimbo-ui migration, or the UI regresses a generation. Number both follow-ups as real stories rather than leaving them as comments, since they become live the moment story 072 broadcasts. In the interim, add a read-only Phase 7/verifier NOTE that logs `DepositPageView.phlimbo()` and `DepositView.phlimbo()` alongside `newPhlimboV3`, so the drift is visible in the cutover record rather than discovered by users.

findings.title: PhlimboV3 and MigratorV2V3 are deployed to mainnet from `via_ir = true` bytecode that no phlimbo-ea test has ever exercised, and story 076's Preflight ticks a `via_ir off` premise this repo does not have
findings.description: `phoenix-phase-2-staging/foundry.toml:1-7` sets `optimizer = true`, `optimizer_runs = 10000`, `via_ir = true`. `lib/phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml:6-15` sets `via_ir = false` with an in-file comment explaining that via_ir caches `block.timestamp` and breaks repeated `vm.warp`. Every phlimbo-ea test and every audit of PhlimboV3/MigratorV2V3 (stories 022-031, audits phlimbo-ea-07..11) therefore validated legacy-pipeline bytecode. Story 076's Phase 4e is the code that actually CREATEs both contracts on mainnet, and it compiles them under phStaging2's via_ir pipeline. Story 076's Implementation Notes assert "Per house knowledge, phlimbo builds use legacy + optimizer with `via_ir` OFF", and its Preflight checklist ticks `[x] ... that PhlimboV3 lands under the EIP-170 24 KB limit in this repo's profile (optimizer on, `via_ir` off)`. This repo's profile is via_ir ON. The EIP-170 purpose of that criterion is satisfied (PhlimboV3 measures 14,529 B here, 10,047 B of margin, `forge build --sizes`), so nothing is blocked — but the tick was recorded against a build profile that does not exist in this repository.
findings.impact: Not an exploit and no defect is demonstrated — via_ir and legacy are both supported solc pipelines. What is demonstrated is an assurance gap at the deploy site: the artifact that will hold user principal is not the artifact the audit and test suites exercised, and the story's own preflight records the opposite. This is a deploy-gate/QA-class issue, not a vulnerability, and its severity should not exceed what that supports.
findings.evidence: foundry.toml:1-7 (this repo) vs lib/phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml:6-15; `forge build --sizes` in workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging reports PhlimboV3 14,529 B / margin 10,047 B, MigratorV2V3 8,248 B. Story 076 Implementation Notes and Preflight checklist item as quoted.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) run phlimbo-ea's PhlimboV3/MigratorV2V3 suites once under `FOUNDRY_PROFILE` with `via_ir = true` and record the result, accepting the documented `vm.warp`/`block.timestamp` caveat by adjusting only the affected tests, or (b) set `via_ir = false` for this repo's build of the phlimbo-ea sources — phlimbo-ea ledger entry V3-L-19 records the measured fact that the legacy build is 15,979 B with 8,597 B of EIP-170 margin, so via_ir is NOT load-bearing for the size limit and can be dropped freely. Independently, correct story 076's Implementation Notes and Preflight tick to say `via_ir` is ON in phStaging2. DISCLOSURE — this is a re-file, not a fresh discovery: phlimbo-ea ledger carries this OPEN as V3-L-19 (Low), fingerprint `38aefbfbe6da599fc5250a2cc73125465c845480e34b6a63984b2febae4a053c`, which anticipated this exact situation from the phlimbo side. RE-FILE BASIS: V3-L-19's own `usefulNegativeResults.v3Unwired` field holds the entry at Low on the finding that "PhlimboV3 has ZERO references anywhere in phoenix-phase-2-staging" and that "phStaging pins lib/phlimbo-ea at 6cb0bc0c, a commit whose src/ predates PhlimboV3.sol entirely". Both statements are FALSE at b9391b1: the pin is f279c62 and story 076 deploys both contracts. The prospective leg V3-L-19 explicitly declined to grade is now real, at a different repo, a different entryPoint, and with a new story-faithfulness component. V3-L-19 also carries an unresolved Low-vs-QA severity dispute for human triage; that dispute travels with this entry and must not be silently re-decided.
